newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials says profits fell 45 percent.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials says profits fell 45 percent.

text.p: Computer chip equipment maker Applied Materials Inc. said Tuesday its profits fell 45 percent in the latest quarter, reflecting lower sales and higher spending.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based company earned $102.1 million, or 54 cents a share, in its second quarter ended in April, down from $185.8 million, or $1.01 a share, a year earlier. Sales fell 20.1 percent to $900.9 million from $1.1 billion.

The results, while down from a year ago, were slightly ahead of expectations. According to First Call, industry analysts expected the company to report a profit of 50 cents a share for the second quarter.
Applied Materials Chairman James Morgan attributed the decline in second-quarter profits to reduced business volume and increased investment in product development.

"We are encouraged by the continued improvement in new orders for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment from the $683.2 million in new orders received in the fourth fiscal quarter of 1996, the low point of this business cycle, to $1 billion in our second fiscal quarter of 1997," said Morgan.

New orders of $1 billion were booked during the quarter, down from $1.3 billion a year earlier but up from $905 million in the first quarter. Backlog grew to $1.5 billion at the end of the second quarter from $1.4 billion at the end of the first quarter.

"The outlook for the remainder of fiscal 1997 continues to be positive and we remain focused on leveraging our resources to better serve our customers' need for leading-edge technology and global support," he said.
Applied Materials reported results after the market closed. Its stock fell $1.19 to $60.44 on Nasdaq.
